{{c|''At the reque{{ls}}t of his mother he vvorketh his fir{{ls}}t miracle, turning vvater into vvine at a mariage in Galilee, although the time of his manife{{ls}}tation be not yet come. 12 Then in Hieru{{ls}}alem at Pa{{ls}}che, being but one, and yet ob{{ls}}cure, he throweth out of the Temple mo{{ls}}t miraculou{{ls}}ly al the marchantes. 28 And being yet of the blind Iewes a{{ls}}ked a {{ls}}igne, he {{ls}}ignifieth {{ls}}o long before, that they {{ls}}hould kill him, but he wil ri{{ls}}e againe the third day. 23 Which al{{ls}}o pre{{ls}}ently they vvould doe, but that he knovving their fal{{ls}}es hartes (though many beleeue in him) vvil not tarie among them.''}} {{dropinitial|A|image=Rhemes New Testament 1582 initial A, two satyrs.png|imgsize=185px|fl={{verse|chapter=2|verse=1}}}}ND {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Go{{ls}}pel vpō the 2 Sunday after the Epiphanie.}}the third day there vvas a mariage made in Cana of Galilee: and the mother of {{sc|Iesvs}} vvas there. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=2}} And {{sup|‖}} {{sc|Iesvs}} al{{ls}}o vvas called, and his Di{{ls}}ciples to the mariage. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=3}} And the vvine failing, the mother of {{sc|Iesvs}} {{ls}}aith to him, {{sup|‖}} They haue no vvine. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=4}} And {{sc|Iesvs}} {{ls}}aith to her, {{sup|‖}} VVhat is to me and thee vvoman? my houre commeth not yet. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=5}} His mother {{ls}}aith to the mini{{ls}}ters, {{sup|‖}} VVhat{{ls}}oeuer he {{ls}}hal {{ls}}ay to you, doe ye. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=6}} And there were {{ls}}et there {{ls}}ixe water-pottes of {{ls}}tone, according to the purification of the Ievves, holding euery one tvvo or three mea{{ls}}ures. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=7}} {{sc|Iesvs}} {{ls}}aith to them, Fil the vvater-pottes vvith vvater. And they filled them vp to the toppe. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=8}} And {{sc|Iesvs}} {{ls}}aith to them, Dravv novv, and carie to the cheefe {{ls}}tevvard. And they caried it. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=9}} And after the cheefe {{ls}}tevvard ta{{ls}}ted the {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ He that {{ls}}eeth water turned in to wine, nedeth not di{{ls}}pute or doubt hovv Chri{{ls}}t changed bread into his body.}}∷ vvater made vvine, and knevv not vvhence it vvas, but the mini{{ls}}ters knew that had dravvne the vvater: the cheefe {{ls}}tevvard calleth the bridegrome, {{verse|chapter=2|verse=10}} and {{ls}}aith to him, Euery man fir{{ls}}t {{ls}}etteth the good vvine: and vvhen they haue vvel drunke, then that vvhich is vvor{{ls}}e. But thou ha{{ls}}t kept the good vvine vntil novv. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=11}} This beginning of miracles did {{sc|Iesvs}} in Cana of Galilee: and he manife{{ls}}ted his glorie, and his Di{{ls}}ciples beleeued in him.⊣

{{verse|chapter=2|verse=12}} After this he vvent dovvne to Capharnaum him {{ls}}elf and his mother, and his brethren, and his di{{ls}}ciples: and there they remained not many daies. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=13}} {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Go{{ls}}pel vpō Munday in the fourth weeke of Lent.}}And the Pa{{ls}}che of the Iewes vvas at hand, and {{sc|Iesvs}} vvent vp to Hieru{{ls}}alem: {{verse|chapter=2|verse=14}} and he found in the temple them that {{ls}}old oxen and {{ls}}heepe and doues, and the bankers {{ls}}itting. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=15}} And vvhen he had made as it vvere a vvhippe of litle coardes, he {{sup|‖}} ca{{ls}}t them al out of the temple, the {{ls}}heepe al{{ls}}o and the oxen, and the money of the bankers he powred out, and the tables he ouerthrevv. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=16}} And to them that {{ls}}old doues, he {{ls}}aid, Take avvay<noinclude>{{rh|||the{{ls}}e}}</noinclude>
